Write $H(\mu)$ for the full entropy of $\mu$ and, for a set $S$ of coordinates in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, write $H_S(\mu)$ for the marginal entropy of $\mu$ on $S$. nodes.title: Shearer's entropy inequality

nodes.summary: For a finite set $\alpha$, a natural number $n$ and a real-valued function $\mu$ on $\alpha^n$, the full (joint) entropy of $\mu$ is $H(\mu) = -\sum_{x \in \alpha^n} \mu(x) \log \mu(x)$, where $\log t$ is the natural logarithm of $|t|$ for $t \neq 0$ and $\log 0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Joint entropy

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, $n$ a natural number, and $\mu$ a real-valued function on $\alpha^n$ with $\sum_{x \in \alpha^n} \mu(x) = 1$. Then the marginal entropy of $\mu$ on the empty set of coordinates is $0$.
nodes.title: Marginal entropy on the empty set vanishes

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, $n$ a natural number, and $\mu$ a real-valued function on $\alpha^n$ with $\mu(x) \ge 0$ for all $x$. If $T \subseteq S$ are sets of coordinates in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, then the marginal entropy of $\mu$ on $T$ is at most the marginal entropy of $\mu$ on $S$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of marginal entropy

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, $n$ a natural number, and $\mu$ a probability mass function on $\alpha^n$, that is, $\mu(x) \ge 0$ for all $x$ and $\sum_{x \in \alpha^n} \mu(x) = 1$. Writing $H_S$ for the marginal entropy of $\mu$ on a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ of coordinates, any two such sets $A$ and $B$ satisfy $H_{A \cup B} + H_{A \cap B} \le H_A + H_B$.
nodes.title: Submodularity of marginal entropy

nodes.summary: For a finite set $\alpha$, a natural number $n$ and a real-valued function $\mu$ on $\alpha^n$, the marginal entropy of $\mu$ on the set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ of all coordinates equals the full entropy of $\mu$.
nodes.title: Marginal entropy on all coordinates is the full entropy

nodes.title: Marginal entropy

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, $n$ a natural number, $\mu$ a real-valued function on $\alpha^n$ with $\mu(x) \ge 0$ for all $x$, and $S$ a set of coordinates in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then the marginal $P_S$ of $\mu$ on $S$ satisfies $P_S(y) \ge 0$ for every $y \in \alpha^S$.
nodes.title: Marginals of a nonnegative function are nonnegative

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, $n$ a natural number, $\mu$ a real-valued function on $\alpha^n$ with $\sum_{x \in \alpha^n} \mu(x) = 1$, and $S$ a set of coordinates in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then the marginal $P_S$ of $\mu$ on $S$ satisfies $\sum_{y \in \alpha^S} P_S(y) = 1$.
nodes.title: Marginals preserve total mass

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
